channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Durigan diz que encontro de Lula e Trump terá em pauta combate ao crime e tarifas
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the meeting between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump this week will focus on combating organized crime and bilateral trade issues, including import tariffs.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 45,3% contra 44,7% de Lula no 2º turno, aponta pesquisa Meio/Ideia
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll released on November 6 shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leading with 45.3% of voting intentions, while President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) has 44.7%, resulting in a technical tie in the 2026 presidential runoff. The difference falls within the margin of error, indicating a highly competitive race between the two main contenders.

item.title: Janja decide não acompanhar Lula na viagem aos EUA
item.description: First Lady Rosângela da Silva, known as Janja, has decided not to accompany President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his official trip to the United States, where he is scheduled to meet with Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday, May 7. Her absence comes shortly after she publicly responded to offensive remarks by Trump’s special envoy for global partnerships, Paolo Zampolli, who referred to Brazilian women as a 'cursed race'. Lula will travel alone to Washington on Wednesday, May 6, and return on Thursday, with a less formal working meeting planned with Trump.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Lula tem maior aprovação no Nordeste e rejeição recorde no Sul
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has higher approval in the Northeast, led by Pernambuco at 61%, while the South and Southeast record the highest disapproval, with Paraná at 60%. Nationally, Lula is disapproved by 52% and approved by 43%, with negative evaluations dominating across all surveyed states, particularly in Goiás (49% bad/terrible) and São Paulo (45% bad/terrible).

item.title: Vídeo: Com licença de Jorge Seif, Hermes Klann assume mandato por SC
item.description: Senator Jorge Seif (PL-SC) took a leave of absence from his mandate until September 2026, and his substitute, Hermes Klann, a businessman, was sworn in as senator for Santa Catarina. The change occurred as permitted by electoral law, preserving the PL party's representation in the federal Senate.

item.title: Eleições: prazo para obter ou regularizar título termina nesta quarta
item.description: The deadline to obtain or regularize a voter ID ends this Wednesday, May 6, 2026. After this date, the electoral registry will be closed until November, preventing those who do not regularize from voting in the 2026 elections. The service is available in person at electoral courts or online via the e-Título system, and is required for voting, obtaining public documents, and enrolling in public educational institutions.

item.title: Pesquisa indica quem os brasileiros querem ver indicado ao STF
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll shows that 39.4% of Brazilians want President Lula to appoint a technical figure with no direct government ties to the Supreme Federal Court. This comes after the Senate rejected Lula’s initial nomination of Attorney General Jorge Messias. The findings reflect public dissatisfaction with politically aligned appointments and a growing demand for judicial independence.

item.title: Comissão debate a redução do Imposto sobre Veículos Automotores
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Constitution and Justice Committee is debating PEC 3/26, which proposes changing IPVA calculation to be based on a vehicle's factory weight, capped at 1% of its sale value. The bill also sets limits on institutional advertising expenses (0.1% of Net Current Revenue) and on legislative and audit court spending, aiming for greater fiscal control and tax fairness.

item.title: Lula é rejeitado por 44,8% dos eleitores e Flávio por 38%
item.description: President Lula has a 44.8% rejection rate among voters, while pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has 38%, according to a Meio/Ideia survey released on May 6, 2026. The poll, which interviewed 1,500 people nationwide, has a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points and a 95% confidence level, and is registered with the TSE under number BR-05356/2026, funded by Canal Meio.

item.title: Eduardo ‘instala poste’ na disputa ao Senado em SP e irrita aliados do PL
item.description: The selection of André do Prado as the PL's Senate candidate, with Eduardo Bolsonaro as his alternate, caused internal party dissatisfaction, as allies argue the move blocks the rise of new cadres and favors a figure close to the Centrão. Despite Eduardo Bolsonaro's absence in the U.S., his surname is being leveraged as an electoral asset to boost the ticket, with the expectation that voters will support André believing he will actively participate in mandate decisions.

item.title: Eleições 2026: cidadão tem até esta quarta (6) para tirar título ou regularizar situação
item.description: Brazilian citizens have until this Wednesday (6) to obtain their first voter title or regularize any electoral pendings. Starting Thursday (7), the electoral registry will close until November 3, 2026, preventing those who fail to act from voting in the October 4 elections. The deadline is particularly critical for first-time voters, those who changed residence, and individuals with outstanding fines or outdated data.

item.title: Conselho de Ética aprova suspensão de três deputados por ocupação da Mesa
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Ethics Council approved a 60-day suspension of the mandates of deputies Marcos Pollon (PL-MS), Marcel van Hattem (Novo-RS), and Zé Trovão (PL-SC) for occupying the Mesa Diretora in August 2025, in protest against Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest and demanding amnesty for those involved in the January 8 events. The decision can be appealed to the CCJ, but final approval requires 257 votes in the Plenary. The defense claims political persecution and lack of evidence, while the rapporteur found a breach of parliamentary decorum.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 53% e aprovado por 44%, diz Meio/Ideia
item.description: A May 2026 Meio/Ideia poll shows 53% of respondents disapprove of President Lula’s government, while 44% approve. Furthermore, 52% believe he does not deserve to remain in office after 2026, compared to 44% who think he does. In terms of performance evaluation, 46.3% rate his administration as 'bad/terrible', 31.5% as 'excellent/good', and 21% as 'regular'.

item.title: Bolsonaro pode ser liberado da prisão no início do ano que vem
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro may be released from closed-regime imprisonment in early 2025 due to a new law reducing sentences for those involved in the January 8, 2023 attacks. STF rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes will determine the extent of the sentence reduction, possibly to 2 or 4 years. Although Lula initially vetoed the bill, Congress overrode the veto, and the PT announced it will appeal to the Supreme Court, albeit with low chances of success.

item.title: Flávio Dino e o alerta do "Elefante Azul"
item.description: Flávio Dino denounces what he calls 'blue elephants' in power — visible problems being ignored, such as the Master Case, opaque parliamentary amendments, conflicts of interest in the TST, and Congress attempting to override the Supreme Court. He warns that this culture of complacency could backfire on Lula in the 2026 elections, as voters may finally notice the absurdities previously tolerated.

item.title: Quaest em 10 estados: desaprovação de Lula é maior no PR, SP e GO, e aprovação é maior em PE, BA e CE
item.description: A Quaest survey conducted in 10 Brazilian states between April 21 and 28 shows President Lula's highest disapproval in Paraná (60%), São Paulo (58%) and Goiás (61%), while approval is highest in Pernambuco (61%), Bahia (60%) and Ceará (58%). Across the 10 states, Lula averages 43% approval and 52% disapproval, with approval exceeding disapproval only in Pernambuco, Bahia, Ceará and Pará.

item.title: Ranking do CLP destaca estado de SP na educação e SC em ações sociais
item.description: The 2026 State Competitiveness Ranking - Elections highlights São Paulo as the state with the best education results in Brazil from 2023 to 2025, showcasing consistent performance over the last three years. Santa Catarina was also recognized for its social actions in the same ranking.

item.title: Maioria não ficou sabendo da treta entre Zema e Gilmar, indica Ideia
item.description: The Meio/Ideia poll revealed that 76.4% of Brazilians were unaware of the public clash between presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) and Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes. Only 10.9% said they might have heard about the conflict, indicating low media visibility of the episode among the general public.

item.title: Flávio tem 45,3% e Lula, 44,7% no 2º turno, diz Meio/Ideia
item.description: A May/Ideia poll released on May 6, 2026, shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) with 45.3% of voting intentions and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) with 44.7% in a hypothetical second-round scenario for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election. The candidates are technically tied within the poll's 2.5 percentage point margin of error. The survey interviewed 1,500 people nationwide from May 1–5, 2026, with a 95% confidence level, and is registered with the TSE under number BR-05356/2026.

item.title: Lula viaja hoje para os EUA; saiba o que esperar do reencontro com Trump
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is traveling to the United States on Wednesday to meet with Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday, aiming to normalize bilateral relations. The agenda is expected to cover tariff barriers, rare earth access, trade investigations, public security — including the potential designation of Brazilian factions as terrorist organizations — and the Pix digital payment system. The meeting takes place amid a tense pre-election climate in Brazil, with concerns in Brasília that Trump may seek to interfere in the 2026 presidential race, while Lula emphasizes national sovereignty in response to perceived interventionist tendencies.

item.title: Com aval do governo, Câmara deve apreciar projeto sobre terras raras
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is set to vote on Wednesday on a bill regulating the exploration of critical and strategic minerals, with federal government support. Reporter Arnaldo Jardim built cross-party consensus and received backing from the Planalto Palace and the PT caucus, aiming for approval before Lula’s trip to the U.S. to use the proposal as a bargaining chip in talks with Donald Trump.

item.title: Lula aposta em encontro com Trump para sinalizar força e tenta se blindar de interferência eleitoral dos EUA
item.description: Lula aims to turn his meeting with Trump into a political asset, using the trip to project international strength and seek informal assurances against potential U.S. electoral interference in Brazil’s 2026 election, particularly through digital campaigns linked to bolsonaristas. While the formal agenda covers Pix regulation, big techs, rare minerals, and trade tariffs, the underlying motive is electoral: leveraging global leadership to offset domestic setbacks, such as the Senate’s rejection of his Supreme Court nominee Jorge Messias.

item.title: Lula se reúne com Trump nos EUA com foco em crime organizado e minerais estratégicos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva travels to Washington to meet with President Donald Trump, focusing on organized crime, trade, and strategic minerals essential to global industry.

item.title: Rejeição a Messias foi a maior no Senado desde redemocratização
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias's nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) was the largest in the Senate since redemocratization, with 42 votes against, surpassing the previous record of 40 votes against Luiz Alfredo Salomão in 2003. The vote followed strong senatorial opposition, with the Senate president playing a decisive role in mobilizing against the nomination, similar to the situation during José Sarney's tenure. Prior to this, six other executive nominations had been defeated, but none with such magnitude, including appointments for ambassadors, the head of the Public Defender's Office (DPU), and regulatory agency directors under the governments of Lula, Dilma, and Bolsonaro.

item.title: Avante lança Augusto Cury como pré-candidato à Presidência nesta 4ª
item.description: The Avante party launched psychiatrist and writer Augusto Cury, 66, as its pre-candidate for President of Brazil in an event held in Belo Horizonte (MG) on Wednesday, May 6, 2026. Cury positions himself at the center of the political spectrum, focusing on mental health, quality education, and emotional development to counter polarization between Lula and the Bolsonaro family. The launch follows the party’s tradition of announcing pre-candidates in Belo Horizonte, as it did in 2022 with André Janones.

item.title: Como PCC e CV representam maior risco para Lula em encontro com Trump
item.description: The meeting between Lula and Trump poses risks for the Brazilian president due to the U.S. threat to classify Brazil’s PCC and CV criminal factions as terrorist groups, which could justify U.S. interference in Brazil and be exploited electorally by Flávio Bolsonaro. The government is actively working with the U.S. on organized crime cooperation to avoid such a designation, while seeking to showcase its own relationship with Trump to counter the narrative that only Bolsonaro has strong White House ties.

item.title: TCE pede explicações ao governo de SP sobre contrato para programa de câmeras de vigilância
item.description: The São Paulo State Court of Accounts (TCE-SP) has requested explanations from the state government regarding a R$ 475 million contract with Prodesp for the expansion of the Muralha Paulista surveillance program, amid suspicions of irregularities in the bidding process and potential favoritism toward the private firm Paladium Corp. The program, which uses real-time surveillance cameras and facial recognition, is a flagship security initiative of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. Allegations claim the Prodesp contract is a backdoor mechanism to benefit Paladium Corp, a claim denied by the SSP and Prodesp.

item.title: Por que foto com Trump pode ser valiosa para Lula na eleição, segundo analistas
item.description: A photo of Lula with Trump could be valuable for the Brazilian president in the 2026 elections, as it demonstrates his ability to engage with global leaders despite ongoing trade and diplomatic tensions. Analysts suggest the meeting reinforces Lula’s image as a statesman capable of defending national interests — particularly on tariffs, critical minerals, and security — without yielding to provocations. The White House visit comes at a strategic moment, aiming to balance external pressures with the need to maintain domestic political autonomy.

item.title: Governo Lula ainda avalia retaliação contra Alcolumbre após derrota histórica no Senado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is still evaluating possible retaliation against Senate President Davi Alcolumbre following the defeat of his nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, Jorge Messias, in the Senate plenary vote. Although he stated he would not act impulsively, Lula has reportedly ordered a mapping of the positions Alcolumbre controls within the Workers' Party administration, suggesting a potential strategic response, even as he rules out an open confrontation.

item.title: Por que Lula não quer que Trump classifique facções como organizações terroristas?
item.description: Lula seeks to prevent the U.S. from designating Brazil's PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, fearing sanctions and unilateral actions. The Brazilian government prefers bilateral cooperation in tackling organized crime, as stated by Alckmin and Planalto aides.

item.title: Mudança na composição do TSE pode levar embargos de Castro a julgamento com novos ministros
item.description: The judgment on the clarification appeals in the case involving former governor Cláudio Castro at the TSE is expected to occur with a different composition, including Ministers Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva and possibly Dias Toffoli, who did not participate in the original conviction. The change in the court's composition may alter the outcome, as the new ministers are not bound by prior positions and could influence the decision on the cancellation of Castro's diploma. Reporter Cueva inherited the case and may delay the judgment, depending on the leadership of the new court president, Nunes Marques.

item.title: Derrota de Lula no Senado é mais um sinal de erosão institucional
item.description: The Senate's historic rejection of Lula's nominee to the Supreme Court signals a deepening institutional erosion in Brazil, reflecting a Congress increasingly at odds with the Executive and undermining judicial independence. This episode highlights fragilities in democratic checks and balances, with potential consequences for governability and public trust in institutions.

item.title: Ficha limpa: destino de políticos condenados está nas mãos de Cármen Lúcia
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia of the STF is analyzing ADI 7781, which challenges Complementary Law 219/2025 that loosened the Clean Record Law, potentially allowing politicians convicted of administrative impropriety — such as Anthony Garotinho, Eduardo Cunha, and José Roberto Arruda — to run in the 2026 elections. The Rede Sustentabilidade party requested a precautionary measure to suspend the law, citing risks to electoral integrity. The case, stalled since November 2025, now awaits Lúcia’s ruling, as she is known for her caution and delays in high-profile cases.

item.title: Acordo por suplência ao Senado não elimina riscos jurídicos a Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: The agreement to make Eduardo Bolsonaro a Senate substitute for André do Prado could be legally invalidated by October due to a STF criminal action for coercion in the case against his father. Experts warn that a conviction before August 15 would trigger ineligibility under the Clean Slate Law, voiding the entire ticket unless replaced 20 days before the first round. The case, opened in February with unanimous support from the STF’s First Chamber, alleges he orchestrated U.S. sanctions against Brazilian judiciary ministers to pressure them.

item.title: Sem Pacheco, PT cogita repetir Kalil em Minas, mas enfrenta resistência interna e do próprio aliado
item.description: The PT views Senator Rodrigo Pacheco's (PSB-MG) gubernatorial candidacy in Minas Gerais for 2026 as unlikely and is seeking to revive talks with former mayor Alexandre Kalil (PDT) as an alternative, though Kalil resists direct alignment with President Lula. Kalil says he is consulting with various political forces and will decide after hearing all sides, aiming to occupy a centrist space in a polarized landscape.

item.title: Lula deve levar a Trump discurso de combate ao 'crime do andar de cima', e aliados falam em trunfo eleitoral
item.description: Lula plans to discuss with Donald Trump cooperation to arrest businessman Ricardo Magro, accused of evading R$26 billion in taxes, as part of the government’s electoral strategy to combat organized and financial crime. Allies view Magro’s potential arrest as a key political asset amid congressional conflict and polling deficits. Vice President Alckmin confirmed the topic will be raised in Thursday’s U.S. meeting, focusing on financial flow control and transnational investigations.

item.title: Após rejeição de Messias, Lula está disposto a mudar critério para escolha de ministro do STF, dizem aliados
item.description: Following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias, Lula is considering changing his STF nominee selection criterion to prioritize candidates with progressive credentials and strong references, even if not personal allies. He aims to avoid further congressional defeats while retaining final authority over the pick, expanding beyond his inner circle. A woman's appointment is seen as desirable, but no favored candidate has emerged yet.

item.title: Lula foca em segurança e economia com Trump e busca virar página de crise interna com ida aos EUA
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will travel to the United States to meet with Donald Trump at the White House, aiming to demonstrate international prestige and counter the influence of Bolsonarists aligned to the former U.S. president. The meeting seeks to advance his agenda on public security and the economy in Brazil, including a possible cooperation agreement against drug trafficking and efforts to prevent the U.S. from labeling Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations. The trip takes place amid internal government crisis with Congress and during the 2026 electoral year.

item.title: Ladrões de cabos poderão pegar até 12 anos de prisão; DF tem 8 casos ao dia
item.description: The Federal District records nearly eight cable thefts of energy, data, and telephony per day, with 5,640 occurrences between 2024 and 2025. A new law signed by Lula increased penalties: cable theft now carries two to eight years in prison, robbery six to ten years, and up to twelve years if the crime disrupts essential public services. CEB IPes reported 21 km of cables stolen in the first three months of 2026, causing R$432,000 in damages.

item.title: Tarcísio aposta em "nova política" para driblar crise com prefeitos
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) promotes a 'new politics' in municipal funding, prioritizing major infrastructure projects over small agreements to contrast with previous PSDB administrations. He claims the government has delivered R$16 billion in 886 road works and that mayors recognize the value of concrete results, despite recent criticism. Allies argue that mayoral support does not guarantee electoral victory, citing Rodrigo Garcia’s 2022 loss as an example.

item.title: Lula e o 'sistema'
item.description: In his May Day speech, Lula invoked the vague and overused concept of the 'system' to explain recent congressional defeats and difficulties implementing his government agenda, avoiding direct accountability. The address was described as uninspiring and repetitive, relying on a worn-out and specious argument to justify political frustrations.

item.title: Lula sanciona com vetos o seguro-desemprego para pescadores
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.399/2026, establishing unemployment insurance for artisanal fishers during the fishing ban period (defeso), equivalent to one monthly minimum wage, requiring biometric registration, CadÚnico enrollment, and proof of activity via the Reap report. The law includes vetoes blocking associations and cooperatives from intervening in benefit allocation and imposes penalties for fraud, such as five-year activity suspension and registration cancellation.

item.title: Lula, el voto del ‘a pesar de’
item.description: Lula is running for re-election in 2026 at age 80, but struggles to generate enthusiasm among progressive voters, who support him 'despite' his shortcomings without feeling inspired by a vision for real change. The threat of a far-right return, led by Flávio Bolsonaro, is seen as even more dangerous than in 2018, due to the current Congress dismantling rights and environmental protections. Without a transformative message, Lula fails to mobilize undecided voters, who seek not just to avoid the worst, but to believe in a better future.

item.title: Lula viaja aos EUA para encontrar Trump; Brasil quer debater combate ao crime organizado
item.description: President Lula travels to the U.S. to meet Trump at the White House on April 7, following a January phone call that revived dialogue. The meeting will cover trade, the PIX attack, cooperation against organized crime, critical minerals, geopolitics, and Brazilian elections, despite recent tensions over the Middle East and diplomatic incidents.

item.title: Prazo para Lula promulgar derrubada de veto do PL da Dosimetria termina nesta quarta; tarefa deve ficar para Alcolumbre
item.description: The deadline for President Lula to promulgate the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetry Bill ends this Wednesday at 7:18 PM. As Lula is expected not to sign the promulgation to avoid leaving his mark on a law he fully vetoed, the responsibility will fall to Congress President Davi Alcolumbre, per constitutional procedure in case of presidential inaction.

item.title: Passagem pelo Salão Oval e comitivas reduzidas: saiba como será reunião entre Lula e Trump
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will travel to Washington on Friday to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump. The meeting will include a brief appearance in the Oval Office for press remarks, followed by a private discussion and an expanded session with up to five aides from each side. Key topics include combating organized crime, preventing new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, and advancing partnerships in rare earth exploration, with Brazil aiming to leverage its recently approved critical minerals regulation bill to strengthen U.S. interest.

item.title: Lula deve usar parceria no combate ao crime para convencer Trump a evitar classificação de facções como terroristas
item.description: Lula aims to use cooperation on organized crime as leverage to persuade Trump not to designate the PCC and CV as terrorist groups, which Brazil views as a threat to national sovereignty. He will highlight an ongoing narcotics trafficking agreement and cite Ricardo Magro, a fuel importer accused of tax evasion living in Miami, as proof that the U.S. also shelters criminals — implying that arresting him would demonstrate U.S. commitment to the fight.

item.title: Lula embarca para encontro com Trump na Casa Branca
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva departs for Washington this Wednesday to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday. The agenda includes Brazilian export tariffs, the U.S. war against Iran, the potential designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations by the U.S., and Venezuela’s political situation. This will be the third personal meeting between Lula and Trump since Trump’s second term began, following prior brief encounters at the UN and in Malaysia.

item.title: Flávio encerra agenda nos EUA no mesmo dia em que Lula desembarca para encontro com Trump
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro concludes his U.S. agenda on the same day President Lula arrives for a meeting with Trump, sparking speculation about 2026 electoral impacts. During his trip, Flávio met with business leaders and bankers to present an economic agenda centered on tax reduction and deregulation, while also discussing electoral scenarios with his brother Eduardo regarding a potential Senate run. The timing coincidence has intensified divisions within Bolsonaro’s base over the political effects of a Lula-Trump rapprochement.

item.title: Lula chega mais 'vulnerável' para encontro com Trump, mas risco de 'emboscada' é baixo, dizem analistas
item.description: Lula is traveling to Washington for an unusually timed meeting with Trump, announced just three days in advance. Despite his domestic vulnerability due to congressional conflicts and declining approval, analysts say the meeting could help him appear more pragmatic and globally relevant, potentially swaying undecided voters. The agenda will likely focus on avoiding sanctions, discussing tariffs, rare earths, PIX, and combating organized crime to prevent U.S. designation of Brazilian gangs as terrorists.
